newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Cabletron founders step aside.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Cabletron founders step aside.

text.p: Cabletron Systems Inc., a major supplier of computer network equipment, said Wednesday company co-founder and chief executive Robert Levine will retire and be replaced by Don Reed, an executive at NYNEX Corp.
Reed will officially assume his new post on Sept. 1, the company said. After a transition, Levine will retire in December.
Levine's departure comes a few months after Cabletron stunned Wall Street with poor quarterly financial results.
In June, the company announced its earnings would fall substantially below Wall Street analysts' expectations, leading to a sell-off that wiped out one-third of the market value of Cabletron stock.
On June 3, the stock lost more than $15 to close just above $30. It has recovered half the loss in the intervening months, but fell 81 cents Wednesday to close at $36 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Rochester, N.H.-based Cabletron was a pioneer in the development of local area networks, which connect computer users within a single department or building. The company remains a leading supplier of network "hub" equipment used to interconnect local area networks.

Cabletron has moved in recent years to expand its focus to include wide area networking products and network management systems used by telephone carriers and large corporations to link computer users across broad geographic regions.
At the same time, Cabletron has lost ground in its core hub business to newer network switching technology, which offers similar functions, but often at lower cost.

Hubs, which require computer users to share network capacity, have fallen out of favour as computer network traffic becomes more congested. Network switching technology can more easily absorb data-intensive transmissions of Internet graphics, voice and video.
Levine co-founded Cabletron in 1983 with Craig Benson, the company's chairman and chief operating officer.
The company said co-founder Benson will continue in his role as chairman, focusing on strategic company issues, while turning over day-to-day operating responsibilities to Reed.
In a statement, Benson praised Reed's experience in running several divisions at NYNEX, the multi-billion dollar phone company that serves the New York and New England regions.

"With the rapid convergence of voice, video and data, Don Reed's extensive telecommunications experience as a 30-year veteran of NYNEX, including service as president and CEO of one of its major operating units, provides Cabletron with expert knowledge in key markets," Benson said.

Reed, a New England native, was named president and group executive of NYNEX in January 1995. Earlier positions incluided president and chief executive officer for NYNEX in New England and executive vice president and chief operating officer of New England Telephone.
Reed will be replaced at NYNEX by Morrison DeS. Webb, NYNEX's general counsel, who will also be nominated to the company's board.

Benson and Levine kept hands-on management control of Cabletron as it grew to become a $1.4 billion concern in its most recent fiscal year. As self-described "owner operators," they defied an industry practice of hiring outside managers as companies outgrow their entrepreneurial beginnings.
From the outset, the two, who funded the company from the profits generated in the course of doing business, prided themselves on never having accepted venture capital.
Levine was the company's chief salesman, but his eclectic, hard-charging management style had met with criticism from some corporate customers who found his approach too brash.
Benson still holds 19.2 million Cabletron shares, while Levine owns 10.2 million, or a combined total of just under 20 percent of the company's oustanding public stock.
The value of those holdings was $1.1 billion based on the closing price of Cabletron's stock Wednesday.
